segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Had Elizabeth’s opinion been all drawn from her own family, she could not have formed a very pleasing picture of conjugal felicity or…” slowly and put it in my own words: Elizabeth reflects that, judging only from her own family, she could not picture a happy or comfortable marriage. Next, craft. I notice the formal phrase "conjugal felicity or domestic comfort," whose grand, ironic sound makes the absence of happiness at Longbourn sharper. The strongest word is “felicity”: a lofty word for happiness, used here for something her parents never had. Then, effect. What does Elizabeth learn from looking honestly at her parents' marriage? My answer: Her father married for youth and beauty and lost respect for his wife; Elizabeth now sees that a marriage without esteem fails, which is why respect will matter in her own choice.
